journey.name: Memory Leak Check - Navigation Loop
journey.description:
Exercises the destroy paths LeakCanary can observe in a single-Activity Compose + Navigation 3 app: Activity recreation and pushing then popping sub-routes. Recreation is driven by a light/dark theme switch, not rotation: MainActivity declares configChanges for orientation/screenSize (PiP), so rotating never destroys it, while uiMode is not handled and recreates it. Switching tabs alone destroys nothing LeakCanary watches. Run against the bench debug build (no sign-in, offline fixtures). The debug build sets LeakCanary's retainedVisibleThreshold to 1, so a single retained object triggers a heap dump and a "leak" notification, and it watches every cleared MviViewModel (Navigation 3 entry ViewModels included).
Known automation artifact: when the journey is driven through accessibility (Studio journeys, `android input tap`, UiAutomator), LeakCanary reports a ProfileViewModel retained via AndroidComposeViewAccessibilityDelegateCompat.currentSemanticsNodes (signature b020956c7d10705657721b2c39790d5fe3ac5780). The same journey driven by coordinate taps with no accessibility client retains nothing, so treat that signature as expected and anything else as a real leak.

actions.action: Verify that the app is open on the Home feed with the bottom navigation bar visible
Tap the first post in the feed to open its thread
Verify that the post thread screen is visible
Press the system back button
Verify that the Home feed is visible
Tap the author avatar or name on the first post in the feed
Verify that the author's profile screen is visible
Press the system back button
Tap the Search tab
Verify that the search interface is visible
Tap the Notifications tab
Tap the Chats tab
Tap the You tab
Verify that your own profile screen is visible
Open Settings from the profile screen
Verify that Settings options are visible
Press the system back button
Switch the device to dark theme
Verify that the app is still showing your profile
Switch the device back to light theme
Tap the Home tab
Verify that the Home feed is visible
Repeat all of the steps above two more times
Press the Home button to send the app to the background, then wait 10 seconds so LeakCanary can check for retained objects

Verify that LeakCanary reports no leak other than the known accessibility artifact described above (ProfileViewModel retained via AndroidComposeViewAccessibilityDelegateCompat.currentSemanticsNodes, signature b020956c7d10705657721b2c39790d5fe3ac5780)
